Page row (dist/index.html and data.js): 'about 1 GJ per flash (published estimates 0.1 to 10 GJ)', status disputed. Fact notes: 'Salinas et al. 2021 (capacitor model): flashes 'most frequently <1 GJ', estimates spanning 10^4 to 10^10 J, the low end biased by their single adjustment factor (their words), so not used as the low bound.'

Source: Salinas, Bruning, Mansell & Brothers 2021. The cited AMS URL gives a CloudFront 403 from this sandbox, but round 1 fetched it with HTTP 200. I read the identical published PDF from the NOAA repository, https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/40137/noaa_40137_DS1.pdf (pdftotext; Crossref confirms JAS 78(12):3909-3924 and the four authors). Section 6a says three things:
(a) 'Estimates of flash energy using assumed, or derived, values of the charge transferred by lightning flashes and the potential difference between the charge regions within which they propagated have showed typical values ranging from 10^7 to 10^10 J of energy (Cooray 1997; Borovsky 1998; Marshall and Stolzenburg 2001)'.

(c) The caveat the notes quote: 'The lower end of the capacitor estimates in this study (<10^6 J) can be attributed to our use of a single representative adjustment factor ... which introduced bias toward larger flashes'.

verdict.reasoning:
I reproduced this. The round-1 fix kept low_si at 1e8 and the display at 'published estimates 0.1 to 10 GJ', and justified it with 'Salinas's own caveat on its low end'. The caveat in Salinas et al. 2021 does not cover that low end. In section 6a the paper says the lower end of 'the capacitor estimates in this study (<10^6 J)' comes from their single adjustment factor. That is about their own model output below 10^6 J only. The same section says, separately, that published estimates of flash energy 'have showed typical values ranging from 10^7 to 10^10 J' (Cooray 1997; Borovsky 1998; Marshall and Stolzenburg 2001). Their reference COMMAS flashes ran from 10^6 to 10^10 J.

So a source the fact itself cites puts the published spread at 0.01 to 10 GJ, not 0.1 to 10 GJ. The fact's notes leave out the 10^7 literature range, and they apply the <10^6 J caveat to the whole low end ('so not used as the low bound'). The round-1 verdict for srclow-1 (gui-c-round1.json) quoted this same 6a passage and gave low_si 1e7 and '0.01 to 10 GJ' as its fix. The outcome applied only the top end.

A second problem stands even on the author's own range: energy_month_of_food_2000_calories still says the lightning rung is 'uncertain by 70x', when 0.1 to 10 GJ is already 100x. With the corrected range it is about 1,000x. 'A round middle value' for 1 GJ also stops being true, since the geometric middle of 0.01 to 10 GJ is 0.3 GJ.

The effect is small. The rung is already rough and disputed, build-data.py rough_fact stays true with low_si 1e7, and ladder.js never reads low_si or high_si. So no comparison on the page changes. Only the stated published range in the sources-table row and the notes are wrong. Minor.
